family_status: EXPLORATORY (new mechanism; no V4 control-arm ancestry claimed or used)
domain: SEC filing-clock instant fundamentals aggregated to the frozen sector cohort: the public-equity valuation-gap channel (filed float vs filed book capital), a filed-facts-only valuation anchor with no price series, no share count and no computed market capitalization anywhere in the signal
mechanism question: Does the sector-aggregate ratio of two issuer-FILED instant facts - dei:EntityPublicFloat (the dollar value of common equity held by public investors, attested by the issuer on its filing cover) over us-gaap:LiabilitiesAndStockholdersEquity (book total capitalization) - rank the frozen 11 sector ETFs by cheapness such that a dollar-neutral book long the 3 sectors with the lowest filed float-to-book-capital ratio and short the 3 highest earns positive after-cost, risk-matched incremental alpha over SPY/sector beta on S0? Causal story: the ratio F_s = (aggregate filed public float)/(aggregate filed book capital) is the sector-level price of public equity claims per dollar of productive book capital. Two forces push subsequent sector returns toward mean reversion in F_s. (i) The valuation channel: expected-return compensation concentrates where claims on book capital change hands cheaply (Fama-French class cross-sectional value). (ii) The supply-response channel: when a sector's public equity is valued richly relative to its book base, the sector's issuers rationally supply equity - cover-page float expands through secondaries and issuance - diluting forward per-claim returns; when claims are cheap, issuance closes and float retires (Lakonishok-Shleifer-Vishny extrapolation/supply reading; Pontiff-Woodgate issuance). The priced object is constructed exclusively from SEC Company Facts instant records: the numerator and denominator are both filing-cover/balance-sheet filed values, so the mechanism is a filed-facts valuation mechanism, NOT balance-sheet expansion (no asset-growth, no size-change input; book capital enters only as the static normalization that defines cheapness) and NOT a price-momentum descendant (the ranking feature contains no price-return term of any kind). Why this exact construction - documented, not hidden: the binding coverage census (packet coverage_census; full census in p2_pit_data_audit_sec.json checks.A7_warmup_coverage) shows that exactly three fields are fundable (pre-S0 availability fraction >= 0.80) in ALL 11 sectors: dei:EntityPublicFloat (min 0.80), us-gaap:Assets (min 0.80), us-gaap:LiabilitiesAndStockholdersEquity (min 0.80). us-gaap:Assets is the balance-sheet-expansion channel, which this wave's channel separation assigns elsewhere; LiabilitiesAndStockholdersEquity is the remaining book-capital normalizer; the float/book-capital valuation gap is therefore the one mechanistically distinct instant-facts channel the authorized census supports. The explicitly disallowed construction - public float versus aggregate MARKET CAP as a valuation anchor - is NOT used anywhere: market capitalization requires price and share inputs that this proposal never reads and never computes. The known internal property that the issuer measures its filed float using a market price as of its own measurement date is inherent to the filed fact itself, is present identically in every authorized reading of dei:EntityPublicFloat, and is disclosed here rather than hidden; the arm's own computation pipeline touches no price series on the signal side.
falsifiable prediction: Directional and specific. The anchor spread - long the 3 sectors with the lowest aggregate filed-float/filed-book-capital ratio, short the 3 highest, 3v3 dollar-neutral, quarterly 63-session cadence - has: (1) strictly positive after-cost expectancy at 10 bps/side over S0; (2) position PF >= 1.10; (3) at least 2 of 3 chronological folds positive; (4) risk-matched excess return positive in at least 2 of 3 folds and overall incremental alpha > 0 versus the frozen risk-matched SPY context; (5) the neighbour (us-gaap:Assets-denominator variant) carries the same sign with positive expectancy; (6) the public-float LEVEL control does NOT reproduce the spread (control expectancy <= 0 AND |control incremental alpha| < 0.5 x |anchor incremental alpha| per the frozen control_alpha_abs_ratio_lt = 0.5 gate). Falsified if the spread is non-positive, if overall incremental alpha <= 0, if the size control reproduces it at the frozen ratio, or if drop-one/turnover/stress gates fail. No post-hoc sign rescue, no denominator swap, no cadence or coverage weakening may be proposed after any scored byte exists.
literature: Fama, E. F., & French, K. R. (1992). The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns. Journal of Finance, 47(2), 427-465; and Fama & French (1998). Value versus Growth: The International Evidence. Journal of Finance, 53(6), 1975-1999 - book-capital-normalized market valuation predicts cross-sectional returns; the primary valuation-channel citation for the anchor's direction (low market value of equity per unit of book capital -> higher subsequent returns).

Asness, C. S., Moskowitz, T. J., & Pedersen, L. H. (2013). Value and Momentum Everywhere. Journal of Finance, 68(3), 929-985 - value premia persist across asset classes and WITHIN industries/sectors; supports the open question of whether filer-fact value aggregates to 11 liquid sector composites.

Lakonishok, J., Shleifer, A., & Vishny, R. W. (1994). Contrarian Investment, Extrapolation, and Risk. Journal of Finance, 49(5), 1541-1578 - the extrapolation/supply reading of value: investors extrapolate growth into expensive sectors and neglect cheap ones; supports the supply-response leg of the causal story rather than a risk-only story.

Pontiff, J., & Woodgate, A. (2008). Share Issuance and Cross-Sectional Returns. Journal of Finance, 63(2), 921-945 - net supply expansion predicts lower subsequent returns; supports the cover-page-float (supply) leg and the prediction that the filed float numerator, normalized by book capital, is the informative object.

conditioning_fields_declared_and_frozen_.declaration_note: per packet binding_rules.aggregation_declaration: the field list and max_filing_gap_days are proposal-level design choices frozen at family freeze and never tuned after scored PnL. 550 days covers annual plus one missed-quarter cadence; a filer whose latest usable filing for a field is older than 550 days drops out by the explicit filing-clock rule in research/assets/stocks/pit_conditioning.py (survivorship-aware; never silent panel trimming).
conditioning_fields_declared_and_frozen_.coverage_floor_rule: a sector observation participates in a decision only if filers_included/filers_mapped >= 0.60 at that decision session; a sector below the floor is held FLAT that decision (deterministic availability rule, not selection). Both fields are census-fundable (>= 0.80) in all 11 sectors pre-S0, so floor breaches are not expected; the rule exists so that behaviour under degradation is fixed ex ante.

PIT observable with availability semanti.store_and_bridge: SEC_EDGAR instant Company Facts over the frozen 410-filer panel (.staging_sec/panel.json; per-sector counts XLB 40, XLC 20, XLE 30, XLF 40, XLI 40, XLK 40, XLP 40, XLRE 40, XLU 40, XLV 40, XLY 40), normalized pit store (store_sha256 f53eb3712bc9d686ec8a91b3715beaf73be1e5243a89af1816bd62eea51df955, 3,817,158 records), conditioned exclusively via research/assets/stocks/pit_conditioning.py (aggregate_sector_asof / conditioning_panel). Sector aggregate = single-vintage equal-weight mean over filers in sorted entity_id order with math.fsum, per the frozen aggregation mechanism; the anchor ratio is the RATIO OF THE TWO AGGREGATES R_s(t) = mean_float_s(t) / mean_lse_s(t), each mean taken from its own gated single-vintage panel at the same decision session (ratio of aggregates, computed at sector level; no filer-level derived field bypasses the canonical bridge).
PIT observable with availability semanti.availability_semantics: SEC filed dates are date-only: availability is the end of the filed UTC day (conservative upper bound); retrieval time never substitutes. A decision at session S reads only records with available_time_utc < 00:00 UTC of S (session_gate_utc; conditioning-lag rule: availability stamp plus one session), regression-pinned by mutation test. Sanitizer totals (conflicting-duplicate facts drop BOTH values, fail-visible; 1.03M of 5.0M raw facts) are constant across all arms.
PIT observable with availability semanti.price_volume_role: the 12-ETF snapshot (37 files, MANIFEST 62ac324d7e683961b0d88f85153e4a072d09fe0a6745a54687b9e3b219d8f658) is used ONLY for leg total returns ({SYM}_all adjusted close), the SPY TR benchmark context and the SPY session calendar. No price or volume field enters the ranking feature in any form.
PIT observable with availability semanti.explicitly_not_used: no computed market capitalization, no share counts (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding is XLC/XLE non-fundable and is not read), no public-float-versus-market-cap construction, no OHLCV-derived fundamental proxy (no_ohlcv_proxy_rule), no FRED/ALFRED/FINRA/Alpha Vantage/ECB/BIS (all BLOCKED or out of scope; any arm reading one fails closed), no other fusion source.

universe/warmup/clock/holding/fills.universe: the 11 sector ETFs {XLB, XLC, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLRE, XLU, XLV, XLY} of the frozen 12-ETF cohort ranked at each decision; SPY is never traded (benchmark context and session calendar only). Rank eligibility is an availability rule: a sector enters the rank set from the first decision at which it has >= 21 sessions of prior adjusted-close history (XLC, inception 2018-06-19, enters ~2018-07; before that the rank set is 10 sectors and XLC is held FLAT).
universe/warmup/clock/holding/fills.warmup: conditioning warmup is certified by the frozen census: both fields have pre-S0 (2018-04-04) availability fraction >= 0.80 in every sector, so the first S0 decision already reads a valid gated aggregate panel built from pre-S0 filing history. Price-side warmup is the 21-session leg-history rule above.
universe/warmup/clock/holding/fills.decision_clock: per fold, every 63rd SPY session starting at the fold's first scored session (offsets 0, 63, 126, ...), decision computed on that session's PIT panel and close; ~10 decision slots per fold, ~30 total across S0 (1842 sessions).
universe/warmup/clock/holding/fills.holding_period: 63 sessions per decision book, weights fixed between decision slots; force-flat at every fold boundary per baseline invariants (the final slot of a fold may be truncated).
universe/warmup/clock/holding/fills.fills: next allowed session after the decision session per the frozen fill clock (no same-session fill); costs charged exactly once per fill.
universe/warmup/clock/holding/fills.book_shape: gross 1.0, net ~0, cash absorbs residual; exactly 6 non-CASH legs per decision (3 long at +1/6, 3 short at -1/6).

anchor + neighbour + causal negative con.anchor: SFV5-A5-H1-A, exact rule (no parameter menu): (1) at decision session t, build the two gated single-vintage sector panels via conditioning_panel(..., field='dei:EntityPublicFloat', max_filing_gap_days=550) and conditioning_panel(..., field='us-gaap:LiabilitiesAndStockholdersEquity', max_filing_gap_days=550); (2) R_s(t) = float_mean_s(t) / lse_mean_s(t) for each rank-eligible sector with both observations present and each panel's coverage >= 0.60; (3) rank eligible sectors by R_s ASCENDING (rank 1 = cheapest); ties broken by ticker alphabetical ascending; (4) long the 3 cheapest at +1/6 each, short the 3 most expensive at -1/6 each; no other legs; weights fixed until the next decision slot; fills next allowed session; force-flat at fold boundaries. Single fixed rule; no scaling, no hysteresis, no vol overlay, no parameter alternatives.
anchor + neighbour + causal negative con.neighbour: SFV5-A5-H1-N, one fixed variant supporting the same mechanism: identical in every element except the denominator field is us-gaap:Assets (also census-fundable >= 0.80 in all 11 sectors): R'_s(t) = float_mean_s(t) / assets_mean_s(t). Same 3v3 book, cadence, eligibility, ties, fills. Mechanism-support logic: cheapness of public equity claims relative to the productive base is denominator-convention-robust; if the filed-facts valuation channel is real, the assets-normalized variant carries the same sign with positive expectancy; disagreement marks the anchor as normalization-specific and the family fails the neighbour-support gate. Not a lookback rescue of any forbidden family: the family conditions on filed facts only and has no price-return, trend or participation term.

causal_negative_control.control: SFV5-A5-H1-C, public-float LEVEL size control: identical surface form (same cadence, book shape, eligibility, ties, fills, costs) but sectors are ranked by the RAW aggregate public float LEVEL ascending - long the 3 sectors with the smallest aggregate filed float, short the 3 with the largest. The control deletes the book-capital normalization and with it the entire cheapness content of the anchor: it is the pure public-float size axis.
causal_negative_control.must_not_carry_if_causal_story_true: if the valuation mechanism is the cause, a ratio-free size rank must not carry the spread after market neutralization and sector-factor removal; any premium it carries would identify the anchor as a small-aggregate-float (size/recognition) effect, not a filed-facts valuation effect. The control CAN fire - sector-level size and investor-recognition premia are live alternatives - which is what makes it an informative falsification surface.
causal_negative_control.preregistered_falsification_rule: the control refutes the mechanism if control after-cost expectancy > 0 AND |control incremental alpha| >= 0.5 x |anchor incremental alpha| (mirror of the frozen control_alpha_abs_ratio_lt = 0.5 gate), or if control incremental alpha > anchor incremental alpha; independently, a negative anchor with a worse control rejects the family per the frozen negative-result rule. No alternate control may be substituted after results are seen.
causal_negative_control.identifiability_by_construction_L7: the control rank equals the anchor rank only in the degenerate case where every sector's filed float-to-book-capital ratio is identical across the cohort; the frozen panel has wide book-capital dispersion (financials, utilities and real estate versus technology), so the ranks are distinct by arithmetic construction. Preregistered pre-scoring eligibility checks (A9-F, PIT data only, no PnL): measured Spearman correlation between anchor and control rank vectors at the decision slots <= 0.90, and at least 25% of decision slots differ in at least one long/short membership leg; if either fails, the control cannot identify and the family is INELIGIBLE before any scoring (lesson L7: V4 lost four proposals pre-selection on measured control self-subsumption rho 0.78-0.83).

incremental-alpha test: Per the frozen benchmark contract: incremental alpha = arm return - risk-matched SPY context, with the SPY context scaled EX ANTE by the arm's frozen risk-match rule: kappa_t = clip(beta_hat_t, 0.0, 2.0), where beta_hat_t is the OLS slope of the arm's own daily book returns on SPY total-return daily returns over the trailing 252 sessions ending t-1 (a deterministic PIT-computable function of the frozen rule; realized volatility is never substituted post hoc). Evaluated per fold and overall; gates: risk-matched excess positive in >= 2 of 3 folds and overall incremental alpha > 0. Sector beta is plausible because the legs are sector ETFs, so the neutralization step is added: daily OLS r_arm = a + b1*r_SPY + b2*r_EW_sector + eps over each fold and over S0, intercepts reported annualized; the anchor must retain positive residual alpha after both-factor removal. The anchor's realized SPY beta should be ~0 by construction; a materially nonzero realized beta is a design-failure flag. Raw PnL, gross beta or long-equity exposure is never accepted as alpha (L6); all gates fail closed.

base and stress costs.cost_schedule: 10 bps per side per fill (base), 20 bps per side per fill (stress rerun), charged exactly once per fill per the frozen no-double-charge invariant (L2).
base and stress costs.both_reruns_reported: the stress rerun is part of the Stage-A gate set (stress PnL > 0 and stress PF >= 1.00); no fee relaxation is available under any circumstance.

turnover and sample floor.convention: turnover = sum(abs(delta_weight)) over non-CASH legs (one named convention, ADJ-5, L3), annualized two-way; both raw and ceiling-normalized reported; frozen ceiling 6.0/yr.
turnover and sample floor.expected_turnover: base case: filed-facts valuation ranks move only at filing cadence, so leg membership churns by ~1 leg pair per decision -> 2/3 two-way per decision x ~4.1 decisions/yr ~= 2.7/yr; plus initial build and 3 fold-boundary force-flat rebuilds (4 x 2.0 over ~7.2 yr) ~= +1.1/yr; base estimate ~3.8/yr two-way, ~63% of the ceiling.
turnover and sample floor.why_inside_ceiling: the conditioning inputs refresh quarterly-to-annually per filer and the single-vintage aggregate is dominated by persistent book-capital levels, so wholesale rank flips between consecutive decisions are rare by construction. Adverse case (2+2 legs replaced at every decision) computes to ~6.4/yr and would breach the ceiling; that outcome is preregistered as an accepted falsification surface of the arm, not a parameter to tune.
turnover and sample floor.cost_drag: ~38 bps/yr at base, ~76 bps/yr at stress; the hypothesized quarterly valuation spread must clear this drag, which is exactly what the after-cost expectancy and PF gates test.
turnover and sample floor.sample_floor: ~10 decision slots per fold (63-session cadence over fold spans of ~607-619 sessions, offsets 0..567) and ~30 total across S0: the frozen floors (>= 5 decisions/fold, >= 30 total, >= 1 non-CASH leg per decision) are met exactly, with zero slack. If any slot is voided (data halt, calendar anomaly, sub-floor sector coverage), the arm falls below the floor and is scored ineligible rather than re-timed. PF is computed over decision-level PnLs under the frozen position-PF convention; the sample is thin but per contract.

drop-one design.drop_one_etf: value_book rerun excluding the single max-contribution symbol by cumulative PnL; the remaining 10 (or 9) sectors are re-ranked from scratch under the identical rule (book still 3v3, membership may change); survival = after-drop expectancy > 0. Meaningful because rank churn rotates membership across periods, so no single ETF should carry the spread; the frozen ETF positive-PnL share <= 0.35 gate is enforced ex post as the concentration backstop.
drop-one design.drop_one_fold: min over folds of expectancy with that fold removed; survival = min > 0. Meaningful because filed-facts value spreads can be single-regime artifacts (e.g. one drawdown episode); the frozen largest-positive-fold share <= 0.5 gate applies as the ex post backstop.

failure interpretation: A Stage-A reject means the sector-aggregate filed-facts valuation spread - filed public float normalized by filed book capital - carries no after-cost, risk-matched cross-sectional information at sector-ETF granularity: either the single-name value channel does not aggregate from filer facts to 11 liquid sector composites, or the measured spread is absorbed by the public-float size axis (control fires), or by SPY/sector beta (neutralization fails). The float/book-capital mechanism class is then closed for this universe and horizon: no denominator swap, no coverage-floor relaxation, no cadence change, no universe subset and no sign rescue is eligible, and the family counts once in the denominator as a rejection. A control-outperformance reject additionally records that raw aggregate float size, not filed-facts valuation, drives any measured spread on this cohort - the honest negative. Nothing in this proposal may be re-entered as a rescue of a forbidden family: the ranking input contains no price-return term, so it cannot be a momentum descendant, and it has no participation, semivariance, calendar or trend component of any kind.

source-to-test map.1: Fama-French (1992, 1998) book-normalized valuation predicts returns -> implementation: R_s = aggregate filed float / aggregate filed book capital, ascending rank, long-cheap/short-expensive 3v3 book (anchor steps 1-4).
source-to-test map.2: Asness-Moskowitz-Pedersen (2013) value works within sectors/industries everywhere -> implementation: the claim is tested AT sector-composite granularity on the frozen 11-sector cohort rather than imported as an assumption; the anchor IS that test.
source-to-test map.3: Lakonishok-Shleifer-Vishny (1994) extrapolation/supply channel -> implementation: the anchor uses the issuer-attested public float (the investable supply) as the numerator, and the prediction is directional (cheap outperforms expensive) rather than risk-scaled.
source-to-test map.4: Pontiff-Woodgate (2008) supply expansion lowers returns -> implementation: cover-page float is the filed supply proxy; the neighbour test (assets denominator) checks the channel is valuation, not denominator bookkeeping.
source-to-test map.5: the priced object must not be sector size or sector beta -> implementation: the public-float LEVEL control with the preregistered 0.5 alpha-ratio/expectancy falsification rule; kappa_t risk-matched SPY context; [SPY, EW-sector] factor intercept neutralization.
source-to-test map.6: novelty and anti-rescue documentation for A7-N -> implementation: at implementation time a feature-correlation check of R_s against trailing 12-1 sector price returns is computed and REPORTED (not tuned): the anchor is expected to be ANTI-correlated with trailing momentum, which is the value identification itself, not a bottom-versus-top momentum inversion - the forbidden momentum entries are price-return trading rules, whereas this feature is built exclusively from filed instant facts and contains no price-return term; the report exists so A7-N can verify that claim against the forbidden inventory rather than take it on prose.
